title: Release Safeguards: Preflight Checklist, Rollback Triggers, and Rapid Comms Templates
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Create a concise, actionable launch safeguards package for the Private deployment rollouts that includes: 1) a deterministic preflight gating checklist, 2) tiered rollback triggers and automated fallback flows, and 3) ready-to-send comms templates (internal, partners, and customer-facing) plus guidance for release note updates. Scope covers hosted release orchestration, Dedicated fallbacks, and Private upgrade procedures. Excludes detailed SRE runbook playbooks (refer to ENG-4823).

Why: Recent canary regressions during model pinning and kernel upgrades exposed gaps in our decision cadence and slowed communications to customers. The goal is to compress detection-to-comm windows to under 30 minutes for P0 incidents and make rollback decisions repeatable across PM/Eng/SRE/Support.

Deliverables: a one-page preflight checklist, a 3-level rollback decision tree, 3 templated comm messages, and an updated release-notes checklist with owners and links to audit logs. These artifacts will live in Confluence (link below) and be attached to release PRs.

Links:
- Draft Confluence doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood/pm/private-deploy-safeguards (draft)
- Release PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-templates/pull/122
- Related SRE runbook: ENG-4823
preflight_checklist: Business signoff: PM and Product Ops (Asha) confirmed feature scope and supported customer list
SLO smoke: end-to-end latency and error-rate smoke tests passing against canary (>= 95% within SLO)
Canary size & traffic: 5% traffic routed, representative queries included in synthetic suite
Model pin validation: pinned model variants exist on target infra and quantization profile verified
Capacity & autoscale policy: Dedicated pools healthy, surge capacity validated (load test artifact attached)
KV cache migration: compatibility check completed, no forced recompute expected
Telemetry & observability: tracing hooks enabled, release-specific dashboards bookmarked, alert thresholds verified
Security & infra: KMS keys present for target account, VPC peering validated
Support readiness: responses drafted, S3 incident bucket for artifacts provisioned, paging roster set
Rollback owner assigned: SRE lead + PM decision owner identified in PR
rollback_plan:
Tiered rollback plan (short summary):
- Tier 1 (Degraded but functional): Reduce canary to 1% and enable degraded-mode fallback (model-variant with lower latency). Trigger: 10%+ sustained latency regression or 3x error-rate above baseline for 5 minutes. Owners: SRE to act, PM to approve within 15 minutes.
- Tier 2 (Partial outage / customer-facing regressions): Full canary halt, route traffic to previous model version or Dedicated fallback pool. Trigger: API errors impacting >2 customers or persistent 5+ minute tail-latency spikes. Owners: SRE executes rollback play, PM notifies stakeholders and drafts customer comms.
- Tier 3 (Severe outage / data safety concern): Immediate global rollback and emergency incident declared. Trigger: data leak, silent failures, or system-level instability. Owners: Incident commander (IC), Exec-level notification.
Steps for any rollback: 1) capture post-mortem snapshot (alerts/log links), 2) flip routing via feature-flag/traffic-router, 3) validate smoke tests within 5 minutes, 4) communicate internal and external updates, 5) open post-incident review and remediation tickets.
comm_templates:
INTERNAL - 1st update (to #releases, SRE, Support, Sales, Execs):
Subject: [ALERT] Private-2026.03 canary degradation detected
Status: Investigating
What happened: Canary traffic showing elevated errors/latency for route /v1/generate since 11:02 UTC.
Immediate action: SRE reduced canary, collecting traces; PM and Support drafting customer messages.
Next update: in 15 minutes or earlier. Links: dashboard | PR | runbook
Owner: Diego Morales (PM)
CUSTOMER - outage notification (short):
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood API (private deployment)
Body: We are aware of an issue affecting some customers using Private deployments. Our team is actively investigating and have temporarily routed traffic to a stable model variant. We will share more details within 30 minutes. If you are seeing production impact, please reply to this message or open a support ticket and reference incident ID: {INCIDENT_ID}.
CUSTOMER - follow-up (resolved):
Subject: Resolved: Service stabilization and next steps
Body: The issue affecting Private deployments has been resolved. We rolled back to the previous stable model variant at {TIME}. No customer data was exposed. Post-mortem will be shared in 72 hours. If you continue to see issues, contact support and reference {INCIDENT_ID}.
PARTNER/SALES - templated brief:
Short note to partner/Sales: We experienced a canary degradation during the Private rollout and implemented an automated rollback. Affected customers routed to the prior stable variant. Expect follow-up from CX with impacted customer list within 2 hours.
acceptance_criteria:
- One-page preflight checklist checked into Confluence and referenced in release PR template.
- Rollback decision tree validated with SRE runbook (ENG-4823) and exercised in one tabletop drill.
- Comms templates approved by Support and Legal (if needed) and stored in PM release folder.
- Stakeholder matrix (owners for PM/Eng/SRE/Support/Sales) confirmed and added to release notes checklist.
- Release PR includes links to dashboards and verification artifacts before merge.
